name: Epic App Orchard
description: Epic App Orchard is Epic's developer and marketplace program for applications that integrate with Epic software. Developers use Epic on FHIR and related Epic integration paths for SMART launches, patient and provider workflows, backend services, sandbox testing, customer implementation, and App Orchard distribution.
agentUseSummary: Connect an authorized Epic on FHIR R4 base URL and bearer token after Epic app registration and customer implementation, then let selected agents inspect discovery and content-minimized FHIR metadata under Safe or Dangerous policy.

credentialRequirements.name: EHR_FHIR_BASE_URL
credentialRequirements.label: Epic on FHIR R4 base URL
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use the exact HTTPS FHIR R4 base URL for the authorized Epic sandbox or customer organization.

credentialRequirements.name: EHR_FHIR_ACCESS_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: Epic SMART/FHIR bearer token
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use an authorized, revocable token from the Epic-approved SMART app registration and customer implementation.

capabilities.label: Read SMART/FHIR metadata
capabilities.description: Inspect tenant discovery and content-minimized metadata for allowlisted FHIR R4 resources without exposing raw protected health information.

allowed.label: Read SMART/FHIR discovery
allowed.description: Read the connected Epic SMART configuration and FHIR CapabilityStatement without patient chart payloads.

approvalRequired.label: Search FHIR metadata
approvalRequired.description: Search allowlisted Epic FHIR R4 resources with Relay-bounded query parameters and content-minimized results.

approvalRequired.label: Read FHIR resource metadata
approvalRequired.description: Read one exact allowlisted Epic FHIR R4 resource through Relay's content-minimized projection.

blocked.label: Expose raw chart content
blocked.description: FHIR narratives, notes, attachments, values, addresses, telecom fields, names, identifiers, and raw records are not sent to agents.

blocked.label: Collect portal credentials
blocked.description: Relay never collects MyChart, Haiku, Canto, Rover, patient portal, provider portal, password, passkey, MFA, activation-code, cookie, or browser-session credentials.

blocked.label: Mutate clinical records
blocked.description: Creates, updates, deletes, bulk export, messaging, ordering, scheduling mutation, and administrative EHR actions are outside this V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Discovery runs directly. FHIR resource searches and reads require approval and return only content-minimized metadata.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Selected read operations run without Relay per-action approval; tenant binding, SMART/FHIR scopes, content minimization, bounds, audits, and token secrecy still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts bounded SMART/FHIR discovery and content-minimized read wrappers; tokens remain server-side.
Railway mounts bounded SMART/FHIR discovery and content-minimized read wrappers; tokens remain server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: Epic requires app registration, production and non-production client IDs, selected FHIR APIs, redirect URI configuration, SMART/OAuth implementation, sandbox testing, customer implementation, and customer IT involvement for organization-specific endpoint access before live use. No provider console, account, credential, consent, Railway deployment, or live tenant validation was performed.
providerSetup.nextAction: Register Relay's SMART/FHIR application with Epic, configure the Railway callback, select the minimum FHIR APIs, complete sandbox and customer non-production testing, connect an authorized FHIR base URL and token, then verify discovery, content minimization, Safe approvals, token refresh/revocation, disconnect denial, and tenant-bound audit records.

evidence.supports: Epic documents registered applications, non-production client IDs, SMART on FHIR, OAuth 2.0, sandbox setup, selected APIs, customer testing, organization-specific endpoints, PKCE guidance, refresh tokens, and backend services.
Epic documents standalone OAuth2 patient authentication through Epic on FHIR rather than collecting MyChart credentials.
Epic's public terms govern use of open.epic and Epic on FHIR developer resources.
Epic documents OAuth 2.0 authorization, SMART launch flows, redirect URI validation, client IDs, scopes, token exchange, and FHIR resource access.
